communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Flock Data Police Use
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the NY Freedom of Information Law, Public Officers Law Art. 6, I hereby request the following records created by or provided to the New York State Police:

1) Between January 1, 2021, and the time this request is received: 
-- All internal and external communications, emails, proposals, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), user agreements, data sharing approvals, contracts, and data sharing agreements, between the New York State Police and Flock Safety (Flock Group, Inc.) or any local law enforcement agency, concerning use and access to the Flock network, the National Lookup tool, and Automated License Plate Reader (“ALPR”) systems. Include sharing settings of Flock databases.

2) Between January 1, 2024 and the time this request is received:
-- All log files or exports for queries executed by State Police personnel involving the search terms, queries, justifications, or codes: “ICE,” “Wanted by ICE,” “Immigration,” “Immigration (civil/administrative),” “DHS”, “CBP,” “Wanted by CBP,” or “Wanted by DHS.” Please provide information in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, agency-level access metrics, search query parameters, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 
-- All internal and external communications, emails, and letters between the New York State Police and the Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (“ICE”), or Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”), regarding cooperation, data access, or data sharing involving Flock Safety or ALPR systems.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michelle Du

title: EO 14399 Voter Data Request (Arizona Secretary Of State - Elections Division)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1) All communications, letters, demands, instructions, and emails between United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (“USCIS”) agency officials, including but not limited to the USCIS’s Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (“FDNS”), and state election officials regarding:
-- The implementation of Executive Order 14399 (“Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections”).
-- Development of a state citizenship list portal, including any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance, concerning the USCIS “Executive Order 14399 Implementation” memoranda directing the creation of infrastructure for state citizenship portals (June 8, 2026), https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053.151.1.pdf. 
-- Plans to transfer personally identifiable data to create state citizenship lists, including receipts showing data transfer between relevant agencies.
-- Implementation of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” The “Unlawful Voter Initiative” refers to the initiative described in the “Disclosure Letter to Senator Padilla from Anonymous Whistleblower re: Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Direction to Identify ‘Unlawful Voters,’” (Sept 13, 2026), https://www.democrats.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/091326_-_senate_whistleblower_letter_dhs_uscis_combined_signedpdf.pdf. 

2) All memoranda of understanding (MOUs), data sharing agreements, or negotiations between state election officials and USCIS officials regarding granting federal agents access to personally identifiable data of state voters or the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.”

3) All log files, export or query counts, and metadata showing access of state voter data by USCIS personnel in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, access metrics, confirmations of attestation statements (that the searcher is the voter or acting with the voter’s express authorization), search query parameters, pseudonymized user IDs, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 

4) Any internal complaints, alerts, incident investigations, audits, communications, reports, or notices regarding suspected violations of state election privacy laws relevant to the implementation of Executive Order 14399, the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” and the creation of state citizenship lists. 

I am requesting these records for the time period of March 1, 2026 to the present.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Michelle Du
